# Affine-multiplier stationarity does not force parity saturation

This actual example has strict proper-closed-minor quotas, a nonaffine fiber-centroid graph, a unique positive geometric-mean multiplier optimum, and regular selected buffered critical caps. Its tilted base barycenter is the sole deepest base, which occupies only ONE of the TWO occupied parities. Most original mass lies outside its deepest-base hull.

No below-OC claim is made: this is a safe one-integer, one-continuous-dimensional calibration of the arithmetic stationarity inference.

## 1. Actual family and quotas

At bases −1,0,1 take

    K_−=K_+=[−1,1],           K_0=[−1,2].

Their convex hull has exactly those integer fibers, because K_0 contains the midpoint of the identical endpoint intervals. Their lengths are 2,3,2, total M=7, and k(P)=2. Every singleton has mass <7/2. Each consecutive two-point closed minor has mass 5<7; the endpoint pair is not closed. Thus all proper closed-minor quotas are strict.

The continuous centroids are 0,1/2,0, a genuinely nonaffine graph. Their volume-weighted within-fiber covariance is

    Sigma=[2^3+3^3+2^3]/(12M)=43/84.                       (1)

Pure integer isolation bounds every buffered depth at either endpoint base by 2, independently of the multiplier.

## 2. Exact all-slope middle formula

Define F(t)=length([-1,1] intersect [t,infinity)). Direct interval clipping gives

    inf_a [F(h−a)+F(h+a)]=J(h),
    J(h)=min{2,2 max(1−h,0)}.                              (2)

For h<=0, monotonicity and F(a)+F(−a)=2 give the lower bound 2, attained by large finite |a|. For 0<=h<=1, if both thresholds are interior their sum is 2−2h; clipping either end cannot reduce it. The value is attained at a=0. For h>=1, a=0 gives zero.

Let U(h)=min(3,max(2−h,0)) and L(h)=min(3,max(h+1,0)) be the upper and lower middle interval masses. At an interior middle mark y, let delta>=0 be its actual continuous threshold buffer. Both continuous normal signs and every integer tilt are then accounted for by

    b(0,y)=min{5, U(y−delta)+J(y−delta),
                    L(y+delta)+J(−y−delta)}.              (3)

The constant 5 is the pure-base depth. Arbitrarily steep tilts in (2) may always be replaced by finite isolating tilts since all intervals are bounded.

With delta=0, (3) yields a unique middle maximum at

    y_0=1/4,          Q_0=13/4.                            (4)

Indeed for −1<=y<=0 the lower branch is 3+3y<=3; for 0<=y<=1 the two branches are 3+y and 4−3y; and for 1<=y<=2 the upper branch is 2−y<=1. Endpoints have ordinary maximum 1. Thus (0,1/4) is the unique original deepest point.

## 3. Positive geometric-mean multipliers and their unique optimum

Every positive affine multiplier on [−1,1] is ell(z)=c(1+bz), |b|<1. Weighted geometric-mean normalization gives

    ell(−1)^2 ell(0)^3 ell(1)^2=1,
    c=(1−b^2)^(−2/7)>=1,                                 (5)

with equality exactly at b=0. The aligned invariant buffer at a middle mark is

    delta(y)=epsilon sqrt[43 c E(y)/588],
    E(y)=3−(4/3)(y−1/2)^2.                                (6)

The middle buffered maximum depends only on c and is nondecreasing in c. Since its ordinary maximum is already 13/4>2, the endpoint bases never compete, for any multiplier. For sufficiently small epsilon, its maximum is strictly increased by ANY increase from c=1: at the c=1 maximizing mark both own traces are proper, so increasing delta first adds a strictly positive own interval length to both orientations, uniformly in the integer tilt. All other contributions are nondecreasing and the pure-base value 5 has a strict gap. Larger increases cannot undo that strict improvement.

The exact calculation below establishes these proper traces for every 0<epsilon<=10^(−4). Hence the UNIQUE multiplier minimum is

    b=0,          ell(z)=1.                               (7)

This is a global minimum over the entire positive geometric-mean affine domain, not a formal infinitesimal stationary point.

## 4. Exact buffered maximizing mark and regular selected menu

For c=1 and epsilon<=10^(−4), (6) gives delta(y)<epsilon/2 on the whole interval. Changing a threshold by delta increases each fiber mass by at most delta; hence (3) differs from ordinary depth by at most 3delta. The strict ordinary gap outside |y−1/4|<1/100 implies every maximizing mark lies in that neighborhood.

There y−delta and y+delta lie strictly between 0 and 1, and the exact two branches become

    4−3y+3delta(y),         3+y+delta(y).                  (8)

In the neighborhood, |delta'(y)|<epsilon. Thus the first decreases strictly and the second increases strictly. Their unique intersection satisfies

    y_epsilon=1/4+delta_epsilon/2,
    Q_epsilon=13/4+3delta_epsilon/2.                       (9)

Put t=43epsilon^2/1764. Substitution into (6) gives

    (1+t)delta_epsilon^2−t delta_epsilon−35t/4=0,
    delta_epsilon=[t+sqrt(35t+36t^2)]/[2(1+t)].             (10)

This also verifies directly that the meeting point lies in the stated neighborhood. The unique deepest base remains 0.

One actual upper critical cap has integer tilt zero and threshold x>=y_epsilon−delta_epsilon. All three interval traces are proper. Two actual lower critical caps are

    x−2z<=y_epsilon+delta_epsilon,
    x+2z<=y_epsilon+delta_epsilon.

Each has a proper middle trace, one strictly full endpoint and one strictly empty endpoint. Therefore a positive two-normal continuous circuit can be selected with either lower cap; the chosen rows are regular in all cap parameters. This is not a supporting-face or zero-coarea example.

## 5. The stationarity condition and its exact limitation

For geometric-mean normalization, infinitesimal affine multiplier variations phi at ell obey

    sum_z V_z phi(z)/ell(z)=0.

The associated tilted base barycenter is

    p_tilt=[sum_z V_z z/ell(z)]/[sum_z V_z/ell(z)].          (11)

At the actual unique optimum ell=1, this is zero by the equal endpoint weights. It belongs to the convex hull of the SINGLE active deepest base {0}; all infinitesimal normalized affine variations vanish at that base.

Nevertheless k({0})=1<k(P)=2, and its fiber mass is only 3/7 of the original mass. The outside fibers carry 4/7 and are not in the deepest-base hull. Thus tilted-barycenter containment, regular selected groups, strict quotas, and genuine multiplier minimality do not force parity saturation or mass exhaustion.

This leaves open any additional consequence of a genuinely BELOW-TARGET jointly attained bad family. Here Q_0/M=13/28 exceeds the d=n=1 target 1/4, so no OC obstruction or low-depth counterexample is asserted.
